messages.author: 7922d8827f75b337
messages.subject: Negative variance warning
parts:
Hi, 
I have a a simple model:

> model4 <- '
+ #measurement model
+ rpm =~ Q05r_typsumtemp + Q05r_waves + Q05r_ pwrhot
+ #regressions
+ rpm ~ Q22
+ #residual correlations
+ Q05r_typsumtemp ~~ Q05r_waves + Q05r_ pwrhot
+ Q05r_waves ~~ Q05r_ pwrhot
+ '
> fit_rpm3 <- sem(model4,dbsem2)

I get a warning message

In lav_model_vcov(lavmodel = lavmodel, lavsamplestats = lavsamplestats,  :
  lavaan WARNING: could not compute standard errors!
  lavaan NOTE: this may be a symptom that the model is not identified.

What could be the reason? What should I check?

I tried
> inspect(fit_rpm3,"theta")

The results of that are as under

                            Q05r_t Q05r_w Q05r_p Q22   
Q05r_typsumtemp  0.899                     
Q05r_waves           0.087  0.698              
Q05r_pwrhot           0.089  0.425  1.498       
Q22                       0.000  0.000  0.000 19.243

I am new to both Lavaan and SEM.

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Negative variance warning
parts: Factor loadings are estimated based on the covariances between observed variables. If you allow residual covariances between all of those same observed variables, then neither the loadings nor the residual covariances can be uniquely estimated. If you want to estimate the loadings, then delete the lines that enable residual covariances.
